newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B index up at noon in quiet trading.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B index up at noon in quiet trading.

text.p: Shanghai's foreign currency B shares rose slightly on Wednesday morning in quiet trading with investors largely glued to the sidelines as they waited for fresh news, brokers said.
B share market sentiment was helped by a gain in Shanghai's domestic currency A share index, which rose on the news that Shenzhen Development Bank would not change its 1996 dividend plan, they said.
The B index rose 0.443 points or 0.59 percent to 75.282 points on volume of 4.820 million shares worth $1.917 million.
Buying of Pudong-related property developer Shanghai Lujiazui Finance & Trade Zone Development Co helped boost the B share index on Wednesday, but overall volume was thin, brokers said.
Investors had sold shares of companies with ties to Pudong, Shanghai's premier development zone, earlier this week on fears of poor interim results, they said.
"I think we could be in for a long, quiet summer," said a broker at a foreign securities firm. "But my feeling is the fourth quarter (of 1997) could see steady gains."
Of 45 B shares, 32 traded with 17 up, nine down and six flat.
Shanghai Vacuum and Electron Device Co was the biggest B share gainer on speculative buying, rising $0.010 or 6.25 percent to $0.170.
Shanghai Refrigerator Compressor Co was the most actively traded on bargain-hunting, gaining $0.010 or 2.50 percent to $0.410 on volume of 857,140 shares.
Meanwhile, the A index moved up 11.563 points or 0.91 percent to 1,276.124 points on volume of 229.848 million shares worth 2.641 billion yuan.
"The performance of the A share market was not bad since the Shenzhen Development Bank announcement had a positive effect," said a broker at Shenzhen J&A Securities in Shanghai.
Investors had feared the bank would scale back its dividend after being fined by securities regulators for illegally trading its own shares.
Shanghai's SSE30 blue chip index rose 45.493 points or 1.18 percent to 3,902.986 points.
The A and B share markets were likely to continue to move in narrow ranges in afternoon trading on Wednesday, brokers said.
